name: Oculosympathetic pathway
modality: pupillary dilation, lid elevation, facial sweating
summary: The sympathetic supply to the eye is a three-neuron chain that travels a remarkable distance: from the hypothalamus down the brainstem tegmentum and lateral cervical cord to the ciliospinal center at C8–T2; out through the T1 root over the lung apex and up the cervical chain to the superior cervical ganglion; and finally along the internal carotid artery through the cavernous sinus and the ophthalmic division to the dilator pupillae and Müller's muscle, with the sweat fibers leaving on the external carotid. A lesion anywhere along this route gives Horner syndrome, and the company it keeps (brainstem signs, hand weakness, neck pain, cavernous sinus nerves) plus the sweating pattern tells you where.

neuronChain.cellBody: Preganglionic neuron in the ciliospinal center

neuronChain.synapse: dilator pupillae, Müller's muscle, facial sweat glands

waypoints.note: T1 root, stellate ganglion, lung apex, cervical chain
briefly joins the abducens nerve then V1
nasociliary nerve and long ciliary nerves to the dilator

termination: Dilator pupillae, superior tarsal (Müller's) muscle, orbital vessels and the sweat glands of the face.

lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Horner syndrome with anhidrosis of the whole side of the face and body; accompanied by brainstem or cord signs

lesionEffectsByLevel.level: Ciliospinal center, T1 root, lung apex, cervical chain (second-order)
lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Horner with facial anhidrosis; hand weakness or pain (Pancoast), neck surgery or trauma

lesionEffectsByLevel.level: Superior cervical ganglion, carotid, cavernous sinus (third-order)
lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Horner without anhidrosis; neck pain (dissection), sixth nerve palsy (cavernous), cluster headache

pearls: Small pupil, mild ptosis, anisocoria greater in the dark: Horner. Where? Sweating and the neighbors decide
Painful Horner is carotid dissection until proven otherwise
Hydroxyamphetamine dilates a preganglionic Horner pupil but not a postganglionic one
